summary: One row of a Menu. A collection element: Menu reads its props and draws the row as `menuitem`, `menuitemradio` or `menuitemcheckbox`.
useWhen: a row in a Menu or a MenuSection — it is not usable anywhere else

useInstead.when: it is a top-level navigation destination
it is a standalone action outside a list

composition.note: A collection element, like TabItem: it renders nothing itself and never appears in the DOM. `key` identifies it to Menu's `onAction`, `selectedKeys` and `disabledKeys`.
composition.example:
<MenuItem key="duplicate" icon={<Icon as={Copy} />}>Duplicate</MenuItem>
<MenuItem key="move" title="Move to"><MenuItem key="archive">Archive</MenuItem></MenuItem>

icon.note: leading icon; omit its `label` — the row's text names it

title.note: only on a row that opens a submenu: the row's label, while its children are the submenu's MenuItems. Submenus open only inside a MenuTrigger

guarantees: the role, `aria-checked` and `aria-disabled` are supplied by Menu from its selection mode and keys, not by this element
the check glyph occupies its slot whenever the menu has a selection mode, so rows never reflow as the selection moves
requires: text in `children`, or `textValue` when the children are not plain text — typeahead matches against it

antiPatterns.why: it renders nothing on its own

antiPatterns.dont: an icon-only MenuItem with no children
antiPatterns.why: the row announces nothing and typeahead cannot reach it

antiPatterns.dont: array indexes as keys in a list that can change
antiPatterns.why: selection and actions are expressed in keys, so the selected row silently becomes a different row

deprecated.note: Put the item's key in Menu's `selectedKeys` and set its `selectionMode`.
